scope: PR-gate security verdict, diff-based, re-keyed to the post-remediation head: feature/0.5.1 -> develop, range origin/main..e9b0a1f2 (4 commits, 9 files, +138/-66). Lanes: OWASP Top 10 over the diff, secrets/privacy over every added line, injection review of the two new subprocess call sites, GitHub Actions workflow review, dependency/CVE lane, governance-record schema validation (RELEASE.json + BUGS.jsonl), subtree-identity proof for the re-key delta, targeted contract-test execution, pre-push denylist gate.
verdict_reason: APPROVED for feature/0.5.1 -> develop at e9b0a1f2035b35ea1558e2bb79b9f32593895be3. This re-keys and REPLACES the verdict previously issued at d9f9685c (same file, rewritten in place; no stale 0.5.1 verdict remains on disk). The re-key delta is provably specs-only: the dadaia_workspace/, tests/ and .github/ trees are byte-identical between d9f9685c and e9b0a1f2 (tree objects 85b0fe19, e8f4ef91, ff5d5366 unchanged), e9b0a1f2's first parent is d9f9685c, and no changed path lies outside specs/ — so every code, workflow and test finding re-keys by identity rather than by assumption. TWO OF THE THREE MEDIUMS ARE NOW CLOSED, verified by re-running the exact validations that raised them: RELEASE.json goes 12 schema errors -> 0 (all 28 log entries canonical; the fix also repaired the 3 pre-existing invalid entries I had only flagged as context), and BUGS.jsonl goes 10 invalid records -> 8, the delta being exactly this PR's two records, whose evidence_diff now carries the mandatory net-positive: prefix and whose diff_direction I independently re-measured (numstat 52/13 = net +39, so net-positive is correct). No blocking security or privacy finding: zero secrets, credentials, tokens, PII, operator-local paths, IPs or private names across all 138 added lines — re-scanned in full because the re-key rewrites archived prose, the shape that can resurrect a redacted value; zero dependency/lockfile changes hence zero CVE delta; no generated-file leakage; no auth or access-control surface touched; workflow permissions, OIDC publishing, environment gates and full-sha action pins byte-identical to origin/main. Evidence at this sha: pytest 35 passed / 0 failed, exit 0 — RE-RUN rather than carried over, because test_resolved_commit_stored_equals_derived.py parametrises over BUGS.jsonl and its input changed even though its own bytes did not; 'dadaia ci push-gate-check' over the pushed range exit 0. BUG-SURFACE AXIS: REDUCED on three counts — the shallow precondition moves from every workflow checkout into the adapter's own contract (+6 production lines, one guard); ratchet suite discovery collapses from 4 private walks plus an exclusion branch into one git-tracked enumeration with the special case deleted; and the governance-record defect class in the touched documents is driven to zero. Counterweight stated in full: production/test line count grew (+46 and net +39), so the reduction is in duplicated call sites and branches, not bytes — and the ledger now says exactly that instead of claiming a shrink. Ten non-blocking findings remain open (1 MEDIUM: the shallow guard raises on a resolver documented as never-raising, though no production call site wires the reader today; 9 LOW, three of them NEW and introduced by the re-key itself: double serialisation baked 13 literal backslash-u-2014 sequences into log[24]'s narrative, structured provenance was folded into free-text note bodies, and two write-once fields were corrected in place out-of-band of the bugs-update seam after the branch had already been pushed to origin — justified and evidence-backed here, but an audit-lane carve-out, not a precedent). None meets the REQUEST_CHANGES bar (privacy, secrets, PII, auth gaps, unsafe dependencies, generated-file leakage). A security report is a snapshot of this diff at this sha, never a statement that the repository is secure.

findings.message: Injection lane clean on both new subprocess call sites: static argv lists, no shell, no interpolated caller input.
findings.detail_md:
Unchanged at this head (proved by the `dadaia_workspace`/`tests` tree identity above).

**1. `dadaia_workspace/infrastructure/git_subprocess.py:444`** (production)

```python
shallow = _run_bytes(["git", "rev-parse", "--is-shallow-repository"], cwd=repo)
```

Every argv element is a literal. `_run_bytes` (`git_subprocess.py:26`) is `subprocess.run(args, cwd=cwd, capture_output=True)` — list argv; `grep -n 'shell='` over the module returns nothing. `repo` is passed only as `cwd`, never concatenated; `pathspec` reaches only the exception message via `!r`, never argv (and the pre-existing `git log` call still places it after `--`). The byte comparison `shallow.stdout.strip() == b"true"` is CRLF-safe, so the guard behaves identically on the windows-latest runners.

**2. `tests/helpers/suite_files.py:19-24`** (test helper)

```python
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "ls-files", "-z", "--", "tests"],
    cwd=repo_root, capture_output=True, check=True,
)
```

Literal argv, `--` terminator, `repo_root` only as `cwd`, no shell. The `pattern` parameter never reaches git — it is applied in-process with `fnmatch.fnmatch` over the basename, so no glob or shell metacharacter is interpreted by an external process. `-z` correctly disables git's `core.quotePath` escaping, so the subsequent `stdout.decode("utf-8").split("\0")` reads real bytes rather than C-quoted octal.
findings.fix_recommendation: No action.

findings.message: OPEN — the shallow guard raises on a resolver path whose own contract documents 'never raising' (A8.3); not reachable in production today, but it becomes reachable the moment the CLI wires the reader.
findings.detail_md:
The one MEDIUM this re-key does NOT address, carried forward unchanged and re-verified against the identical `dadaia_workspace` tree.

`dadaia_workspace/features/bugs/service.py:228-263` documents `BugService.resolved_commit` as degrading to "stored or `None`", **"never raising and never a new blocking validation (A8.3)"**. It calls `self._history_reader.log_added_lines(...)` at `service.py:260` with no `try`. As of `git_subprocess.py:444-450` that call raises `GitHistoryReadError` whenever the repo is shallow, so the resolver's documented no-raise contract no longer holds for the shallow case.

**Not reachable in production at this sha** — verified: `container.build_git_history_reader()` (`container.py:216`) has zero call sites outside `tests/`, and no CLI module references `migrate_v5` / `run_migration`. Every current construction site passes neither `history_reader` nor `repo_root`, so the method short-circuits to `None` before any git walk.

**Why it still matters:** `container.py:216`'s own docstring names the CLI composition root as the intended next caller. On that day, a consumer whose workspace repo is a `git clone --depth 1` (a container image, a CI checkout, a bandwidth-constrained install) gets an uncaught `GitHistoryReadError` out of a read-only `bugs status`/`bugs stats` render instead of the documented `None` degrade — an availability regression on a display path.

Reproduce: `git clone --depth 1 file://<repo> /tmp/shallow`, then construct `BugService(..., history_reader=container.build_git_history_reader(), repo_root=Path('/tmp/shallow'))` and call `.resolved_commit(record)` on any record whose `resolved_commit is None`.
findings.fix_recommendation: Design call for software-architect + software-engineer, not for this PR: decide, once, whether the shallow condition is fatal (keep the raise; amend `service.py`'s A8.3 docstring and have the future CLI caller catch it and render a warning) or degradable (catch `GitHistoryReadError` in `BugService.resolved_commit` and return `None`, keeping loudness for the migration/contract-test callers). Do NOT resolve it by adding a flag or a second code path through the adapter.

findings.message: OPEN — the shallow guard is fail-open: a non-zero `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` exit silently restores the exact silent-under-report behaviour the guard exists to prevent.
findings.detail_md:
`dadaia_workspace/infrastructure/git_subprocess.py:444-450`

```python
shallow = _run_bytes(["git", "rev-parse", "--is-shallow-repository"], cwd=repo)
if shallow.returncode == 0 and shallow.stdout.strip() == b"true":
    raise GitHistoryReadError(...)
```

The `returncode == 0` conjunct means any git that does not understand the flag (added in git 2.15, 2017) — or any unexpected rev-parse failure — falls through to the walk and produces the partial, plausible-looking history the guard was written to refuse. This is the opposite posture from the sibling error path in the same method, which fails CLOSED on a non-zero exit (`git_subprocess.py:465-470`).

Blast radius is small today: the runner images and the local toolchain (git 2.43.0) support the flag, and a non-repo path fails closed one call later at the `git log` guard. The exposure is a consumer on an old or minimal git image, where the silent-wrong-data mode returns unannounced.
findings.fix_recommendation: Make the guard fail closed like its sibling — `if shallow.returncode != 0 or shallow.stdout.strip() == b"true": raise GitHistoryReadError(...)`, with the message distinguishing 'shallow' from 'cannot determine depth'. One line, no new branch for callers.

findings.message: NEW, introduced by the re-key: double serialisation baked 13 literal `\u2014` escape sequences into log[24]'s narrative — the archived qa-close text now reads `not most \u2014 rc-1` instead of an em dash.
findings.detail_md:
`specs/releases/_archive/0.5.0/RELEASE.json`, `log[24]` (the qa-close entry, `kind: "note"`).

The normalisation moved the old `data` object into `text` by `json.dumps`-ing it into a string. Because `d3a95db5` had already re-serialised the file with `ensure_ascii=True`, the source strings already carried `\u2014` escapes; serialising them a second time escaped the backslash, so the decoded text now contains the literal 6-character sequence `\u2014` where an em dash belongs.

Measured on the decoded document at `e9b0a1f2`:

| entry | `len(text)` | literal `\u` sequences | real em dashes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `log[24]` | 7 374 | **13** | **0** |
| `log[25]` / `[26]` / `[27]` | 366 / 276 / 221 | 0 | 0 |

No data is lost and the document is schema-valid; the damage is legibility of an archived governance record that the audit lane reads as evidence. It is also a one-way ratchet: each further re-serialisation doubles the escaping again.
findings.fix_recommendation: product-engineer decodes `log[24]`'s text once (`json.loads` the embedded string, or a targeted `\u2014` -> em-dash replacement) and rewrites the entry with `ensure_ascii=False`. Fix it before the next write to this file, since the escaping compounds. Non-blocking.

findings.message: NEW, introduced by the re-key: machine-readable provenance (rc, sha, pr, merge, phase) was folded into free-text `text`, so fields that used to be parseable now require prose parsing.
findings.detail_md:
The normalisation preserved the old `data` values by appending them as a JSON blob at the end of the prose string. At `e9b0a1f2`:

- `log[25]` (`kind: "rc"`) ends `… cleared by those fixes. {"rc": 1, "sha": "48d032dca6d6b4ceab3f0aea6e25cc68644bad8d", "pr": 219, "merge": "be4b2cc2"}`
- `log[26]` (`kind: "phase"`) ends `… decisions.jsonl). {"phase": "ARCHIVED"}`
- `log[27]` (`kind: "shipped"`) ends `… withheld by operator order. {"sha": "9ebefd5f", "pr": 221}`

This is schema-COMPLIANT — `release-state-v1` explicitly calls `log` "the one place free-form governance narrative survives" and gives it no structured sub-fields — and **no value was lost**, which is why this is LOW and not a regression of the finding it resolves. The `rc-1` merge sha `48d032dc…` and merge commit `be4b2cc2` in particular now exist only inside a string.

Note the top-level milestones (`defined`/`implemented`/`shipped`/`audited`) remain the typed, queryable home for the sha-bearing facts, so nothing an automated consumer needs is trapped in prose — this is a provenance-ergonomics observation, not a data loss.
findings.fix_recommendation: No change requested. If any consumer ever needs `log[25]`'s rc sha programmatically, read it from the `implemented` milestone instead of parsing the note — that is what the typed field is for. Flag for the audit lane only.

findings.message: NEW — two write-once governance fields were corrected in place, out-of-band of the `bugs update` seam that refuses such a re-set by design, after the branch had already been pushed to origin.
findings.detail_md:
The coordinator's own account: *"the CLI `bugs update` refuses write-once re-sets (A2.2b), so the two records this branch itself created were corrected in place in BUGS.jsonl"*.

`bug-record-v1.schema.json` marks both changed fields `"x-mutability": "write-once"` (`evidence_diff`, `diff_direction`). The CLI enforces that; a text edit to the JSONL does not, because `specs/bugs/**` is an ADDITIVE path whose record contract DADAIA.md §3.2 states is **"audited, not gated"**. So this correction is precisely the class of event the audit lane exists to catch, and it should appear there as a ratified carve-out rather than pass unremarked.

One factual correction to the justification, for the record: the pre-correction values did NOT stay local to the branch — `git rev-parse origin/feature/0.5.1` is `e9b0a1f2`, and the branch was published at `202064b3` and `d9f9685c` before that, so the wrong `diff_direction` was pushed. It was never merged to `develop`/`main` and no consumer read it, so the practical impact is nil and I do not contest the fix — a truthful record is worth more here than an untouched-but-wrong one.

Recorded because the alternative reading is the dangerous one: that a write-once field is editable whenever the CLI is inconvenient. It is not.
findings.fix_recommendation: project-auditor records this as a dispositioned carve-out in the next audit window (bug-history pillar), naming the two record ids and this sha. If in-branch correction of a not-yet-merged record is intended to be legitimate, product-engineer should give `bugs update` an explicit, evidence-bearing amend path so the next correction goes through the seam rather than around it — do not leave the seam as something to be bypassed.

findings.message: OPEN — ratchet scope narrows from the working tree to the git index: an unstaged new test file is now outside all four ratchets, and the ratchets stop working outside a git checkout.
findings.detail_md:
`tests/helpers/suite_files.py::tracked_test_files` defines the suite as `git ls-files -- tests`, and four walks now use it: `test_test_suite_ratchets.py:136` (v26 private-symbol), `:199` (v27 intent-header coverage), `:264` (v28 scaffold expiry) and `test_frozen_clock_aging_ratchet.py:113` (`_test_files`). Previously each walked the filesystem.

1. **Untracked == invisible.** A newly authored test file never `git add`ed is outside every ratchet, including the stewardship gates (intent-header coverage, SCAFFOLD expiry) that exist to catch undeclared tests at birth (DADAIA.md §7.2). A local `dadaia ci preflight` can go green on a file CI will later ratchet. CI is unaffected — it always runs on a committed tree — and `git ls-files` reads the INDEX, so a merely-staged file still counts; the window is authored-but-never-staged only.
2. **git becomes a test dependency.** `check=True` means the four ratchets raise `CalledProcessError` rather than skipping when run outside a git checkout. Low impact: poetry packages only `dadaia_workspace` (`pyproject.toml:7`), so `tests/` never ships in the wheel.

Recorded because it is a genuine narrowing of a quality gate's scope the commit message does not call out; it is a deliberate, defensible trade (it is what makes scratch probes out-of-scope by construction), not a defect.
findings.fix_recommendation: No change requested. If the authored-but-unstaged window matters, add a pre-commit warning rather than re-adding a filesystem walk — do not reintroduce per-ratchet exclusion branches, which is the shape this fix correctly deleted.

findings.message: No generated-file leakage: the new test's scratch probe is written into an already-gitignored directory and cannot be swept into a commit.
findings.detail_md:
`test_ratchet_scope_is_the_tracked_suite_never_a_tests_tmp_probe` (`tests/contract/test_test_suite_ratchets.py:505-515`) writes `tests/tmp/_ratchet_scope_probe.py` inside the source tree and removes it in a `finally`.

- `.gitignore:73-74` is `tests/tmp/*` + `!tests/tmp/README.md`; `git check-ignore -v tests/tmp/_probe.py` confirms the rule matches. A probe left by a SIGKILLed run is untracked AND ignored, so it cannot be captured even by a blanket `git add -A`, and `git ls-files` — the helper's own definition of scope — excludes it by construction.
- `tests/tmp/` exists in the tree (carrying only `README.md`), so `write_text` cannot fail on a missing parent.
- The probe name is distinct from the older sibling's (`_ratchet_probe_marker.py`) and from `test_stewardship_mechanics.py`'s pid-suffixed probe, so no fixed-path collision between concurrent xdist workers is introduced.

Confirmed empirically at the previous head: `pytest -n 2` on both ratchet files -> 11 passed, exit 0, `git status` clean. `tests/` is byte-identical at this head, so that evidence transfers by tree identity.
findings.fix_recommendation: No action.

findings.message: OPEN — duplicated invariant plus a slightly more brittle teardown: two tests assert the same tests/tmp exclusion through the same helper, and the new one drops `missing_ok=True`.
findings.detail_md:
`test_frozen_clock_aging_ratchet.py:199 test_test_files_excludes_tests_tmp_scratch_directory` and the new `test_test_suite_ratchets.py:505 test_ratchet_scope_is_the_tracked_suite_never_a_tests_tmp_probe` now assert the same invariant, both reaching `tracked_test_files` (the older one through the `_test_files` shim this change reduced to a delegation). After the refactor the invariant has ONE implementation, so one test is redundant coverage of the other.

Teardown asymmetry: the older test uses `probe.unlink(missing_ok=True)`; the new one uses bare `probe.unlink()`, so if anything else removes the probe first the `finally` raises and masks the real assertion outcome.
findings.fix_recommendation: qa-engineer disposition under test stewardship (DADAIA.md §7.2): keep the invariant at the helper (a small unit test on `tracked_test_files`) and retire the duplicate; add `missing_ok=True` in the same pass. Pruning is a qa-engineer verdict and execution is software-engineer's — never mine.

findings.message: Strict UTF-8 decode of `git ls-files -z` output is correct but unguarded, unlike the decode doctrine the same repo applies to ledger reads.
findings.detail_md:
`tests/helpers/suite_files.py:25` does `result.stdout.decode("utf-8").split("\0")`. Because `-z` is passed, git emits raw path bytes with no `core.quotePath` escaping, so a strict decode is right and no octal-unquoting is needed. A tracked filename that is not valid UTF-8 (legal on Linux) would raise `UnicodeDecodeError` and take out four ratchets at once.

Contrast with the production doctrine in `git_subprocess.py::_decode_lines_strict`, which decodes per line and SKIPS + logs an undecodable line rather than aborting. Not a defect — every path in `tests/` is ASCII and this is a test helper, not a production port — recorded so the asymmetry is a known one.
findings.fix_recommendation: No action; revisit only if a non-ASCII test path is ever introduced.

findings.message: OPEN — gitleaks (secret-scan.yml) never runs on a `feature/* -> develop` PR, so this PR gets no automated secret scan in CI.
findings.detail_md:
`.github/workflows/secret-scan.yml` triggers on `push: branches: [main, 'hotfix/v*']` and `pull_request: branches: [main]` only. The PR under review targets `develop`, so the gitleaks job is not in its check set. Pre-existing gap, untouched by this diff, applying to EVERY feature->develop PR — the edge where new code first becomes reviewable.

Compensating controls exercised at this head: the added-line secret/privacy scan (0 matches over 138 lines) and `dadaia ci push-gate-check` (exit 0). Both are session-local; neither is enforced by CI on this edge.
findings.fix_recommendation: software-engineer adds `develop` to `secret-scan.yml`'s `pull_request.branches` so gitleaks gates the first publication edge, not only the deploy edge. Route as a backlog/bug item via project-manager.

findings.message: Workflow lane: no permission, secret, token or action-pin change; `fetch-depth: 0` cannot reach a published artifact.
findings.detail_md:
`.github` is byte-identical to the previously reviewed head, so this carries over by tree identity.

The entire workflow diff against `origin/main` is six identical `with: fetch-depth: 0` blocks on the `unit-fast`, `contract-coverage`, `integration`, `e2e-python`, `e2e-panel` and `build` checkouts of `release.yml`.

findings.message: Bug-surface axis: REDUCED, now on three counts — two duplicated-precondition classes collapsed to one definition each, plus a governance-record defect class driven to zero.
findings.detail_md:
The standing operator rule's required statement, with ledger evidence. **All three are the same move: stop repeating a rule per call site; state it once.**

**Axis 1 — shallow history (`202064b3`).** Prior fix `contract-coverage-ci-shallow-checkout-collapses-resolved-commit-derivation-to-head` recorded `solution: "every ci.yml checkout runs with fetch-depth 0"` (+28 lines over 14 checkouts) — a per-call-site patch that left the class (an adapter that accepts a shallow repository and returns a partial walk that looks complete) alive. Recurrence: `release-workflow-shallow-checkout-collapses-resolved-commit-derivation-to-head`, `caused_by` that record, same symptom from a different yaml file — Release run 33202885086 on main `9ebefd5f`, 20 FAILED, every derived `resolved_commit == HEAD`. This fix states the precondition ONCE inside `GitSubprocessClient.log_added_lines` (+6 production lines, zero new caller-visible branches), covering both production callers by construction.

**Axis 2 — ratchet scope (`d9f9685c`).** Prior fix `frozen-clock-ratchet-scans-tests-tmp-scratch-dir` excluded `tests/tmp` inside ONE walker. Recurrence: `v26-ratchet-scans-tests-tmp-scratch-dir-xdist-race`, CI run 33203537800 at `202064b3`, `FileNotFoundError tests/tmp/_quarantine_probe_<pid>.py`, because three other walks kept their own raw `rglob`/`glob`. Its `root_cause` names the structure exactly: *"Each ratchet re-implemented suite discovery, so the exclusion had to be repeated per walker — it was not."* This fix replaces 4 private walks with 1 shared enumeration and **deletes** the special-case exclusion branch instead of copying it three more times.

**Axis 3 — governance records (`e9b0a1f2`).** The re-key did not merely patch the two records I flagged: it took `RELEASE.json` from 12 schema errors to **0** (fixing 3 pre-existing invalid entries I had only noted as context) and `BUGS.jsonl` from 10 invalid records to **8** (exactly this PR's two). The defect class in the touched document is now empty rather than reduced.

| axis | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| shallow precondition, places stated | every checkout in every workflow, forever | 1 (the adapter) |
| ratchet suite discovery, implementations | 4 private walks + 1 exclusion branch | 1 helper, branch deleted |
| RELEASE.json schema errors | 12 | 0 |
| BUGS.jsonl invalid records | 10 | 8 (all pre-existing) |
| new caller-visible branches/flags/parameters | — | 0, all three commits |
| shallow-tree failure mode | 20 plausible-but-wrong derivations | 1 self-describing error |
| xdist scratch-probe failure mode | FileNotFoundError mid-scan | out of scope by construction |

No fix adds a flag, a special case, a second code path, a cross-feature reach-in or shared mutable state; each lands inside the unit that owns the contract it defends. **Bug surface REDUCED on every axis.**

Honest counterweight, so the claim is checkable rather than rhetorical: production/test line count GREW (+46 for `202064b3`; net +39 for `d9f9685c`) — the reduction is in duplicated call sites and branches, not bytes, and the ledger now says so in its own `evidence_diff` instead of claiming a shrink. The 6 `release.yml` edits do repeat the per-call-site pattern, but they are now belt-and-braces: a missed checkout announces itself on the first run. And the residual MEDIUM (a raise on a documented never-raising resolver) is a small NEW surface this PR opened — real, unmerged into any consumer path, and named above.
findings.fix_recommendation: No action. Record the axis in the release ledger and prefer this shape — precondition inside the owning unit's own contract, duplicated discovery collapsed to one definition — for the next recurrence of a per-call-site patch.

findings.message: Test hygiene clean: hermetic tmp_path repository, repo-local git config, self-created clone source, no network.
findings.detail_md:
`tests/contract/test_git_history_reader_log_added_lines.py::test_log_added_lines_refuses_a_shallow_repository`

- The clone source is a repository the test itself creates under `tmp_path` in the same function, reached via `origin.as_uri()` (`file://`). No untrusted repository is ever cloned, so the local-clone code-execution class (CVE-2024-32004 and neighbours, which require a maliciously crafted source repo) does not apply.
- No network egress: `file://` transport only; marked `pytest.mark.slow`, runs under `tmp_path`, never inside the source tree (DADAIA.md §5.3).
- Identity is set with repo-local `git config` (no `--global`), leaving the runner's and operator's git identity untouched. The only address-shaped string is the reserved-TLD `test@example.invalid`.
- `subprocess.run(..., capture_output=True)` throughout: no git output reaches the test log.
- Asserts on the exception class and the substring `"shallow"`, not on the absolute path the message interpolates — so the message can be redacted later without breaking the test.
findings.fix_recommendation: No action.

findings.message: OPEN — the new `GitHistoryReadError` message interpolates the absolute repository path, which can carry an operator-local path into a report, log or ledger field.
findings.detail_md:
`dadaia_workspace/infrastructure/git_subprocess.py:446-450`:

```python
f"{repo} is a shallow repository: a history walk over {pathspec!r} would ..."
```

`repo` is an absolute `Path`, so on a developer machine the message renders an operator home path. DADAIA.md §7.3 requires local paths, hostnames and private names to be redacted from every bug-ledger field, and an unhandled traceback is a common route for such a string into a pasted repro, a CI log or a `symptom` field.

Rated LOW deliberately: the pattern is pre-existing and consistent — the sibling error twenty lines below does the same — so this diff adds a new instance, not a new class. The repo is private and no credential is interpolated.

findings.message: OPEN, not addressed by the re-key (and not requested): `shipped.sha` remains the 8-hex abbreviation `9ebefd5f` while every sibling milestone carries a full 40-hex sha.
findings.detail_md:
`specs/releases/_archive/0.5.0/RELEASE.json` -> `shipped.sha = "9ebefd5f"`, and the same abbreviated value in `specs/releases/_archive/releases_histo.jsonl`'s shipped record, versus e.g. `audited.sha = "5c0448dcc1feeec204e24b4b4583618017f6c52b"` in the same document. Confirmed still present at `e9b0a1f2` — the re-key touched only the `log` array.

`release-state-v1.schema.json` places no length/pattern constraint on milestone `sha`, so this is schema-legal — but an abbreviated sha is an ambiguity-prone evidence anchor: abbreviations are not stable as a repo grows, and every sha-consuming gate here is written for 40-hex (`.github/scripts/pr-verdict-check.sh` shape-checks `PR_HEAD_SHA` as 40-hex before it reaches any git argv). Provenance a gate cannot ingest verbatim is weak provenance.
findings.fix_recommendation: product-engineer back-fills the full 40-hex sha in both `RELEASE.json` `shipped.sha` and the `releases_histo.jsonl` shipped record; tighten the schema's milestone `sha` to `^[0-9a-f]{40}$` so the next writer cannot abbreviate. Non-blocking.

findings.message: Commit-message accuracy note: `e9b0a1f2`'s subject claims `specs/AGENTS.md refreshed to canonical template`, but that path is not in the commit.
findings.detail_md:
`git diff --name-only d9f9685c..e9b0a1f2` returns exactly `specs/bugs/BUGS.jsonl` and `specs/releases/_archive/0.5.0/RELEASE.json`. The coordinator's brief said `dadaia specs doctor --fix` refreshed `specs/AGENTS.md` TREE-5 *"if it differed"* — it evidently did not differ, so the tool correctly wrote nothing, but the commit subject asserts a change that the tree does not contain.

Zero security impact; recorded because commit subjects are the audit lane's cheapest index into what a commit did, and a subject that overstates its own diff degrades that index. This is the same evidence-integrity concern as the two record findings above, one layer out.
findings.fix_recommendation: No action on this commit (amending a pushed commit costs more than the inaccuracy). Prefer subjects that describe the realised diff; where a `--fix` invocation is a no-op, say so or omit the clause.

decisions_required: VERDICT PLACEMENT (blocks the CI security-verdict-gate): this handoff lives only under .dadaia/handoff/, which is gitignored, so .github/scripts/pr-verdict-check.sh cannot see it. The gate stays red until an operator/PM commits a copy on feature/0.5.1 at specs/releases/<id>/verdicts/e9b0a1f2035b35ea1558e2bb79b9f32593895be3.handoff.json.
